description: When satellites pass over a place in the next ten days, in the place's local time: for one satellite, every pass with its rise, highest point and set, and whether it can be seen; with no satellite named, the passes a person can see with the naked eye (the ISS, Tiangong, Hubble and the other bright ones), soonest first. Call it when someone asks when they can see the ISS or any satellite from a city, or what passes over them tonight. Name the place (a city: Madrid, Brisbane, Buenos Aires, in English or Spanish) and the answer uses that place's time zone; or give latitude and longitude, and the answer is in UTC unless time_zone names a zone. A name several cities share is computed for the largest, and the answer names the others so you can ask again for one of them. Passes are predictions from the latest orbit data; a visible pass is one in a dark sky with the satellite in sunlight, at least ten degrees up and bright enough; it says nothing about clouds. It cannot answer for a geostationary satellite, which never rises or sets, and the place name or coordinates sent are computed with and never stored or logged.

language.description: The language of the answer and of the page it links: en (the default) or es

latitude.description: Degrees north, when no place is named; with longitude.

longitude.description: Degrees east, when no place is named; with latitude.

place.description: The place's name, a city in English or Spanish (Madrid, Brisbane, Ciudad de México), or one of the alternatives a previous answer named (Portland, Maine, United States). Leave it out to give latitude and longitude instead.

satellite.description: One satellite's alias (iss, hubble, tiangong) or catalogue number, for its passes alone; leave it out for every satellite visible to the naked eye.

time_zone.description: An IANA time zone (Europe/Madrid, America/New_York) for the times of an answer by latitude and longitude; UTC when left out. A named place uses its own zone and ignores this.

name: passes
title: Passes over a place
